# Configuration reference

Every environment variable the gateway reads. `.env.example` declares the same set. A variable set to an empty value counts as unset.

| Variable | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development`, `test`, `production` | no | `production` | Runtime mode. Unset or empty means production, so a deployment that forgets it gets the strict checks instead of the development ones; set development for a local run |
| `HOST` | string, 1 character or more | no | `0.0.0.0` | Interface the HTTP server binds to |
| `PORT` | integer, 1 to 65535 | no | `3000` | Port the HTTP server listens on |
| `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `120000` | Milliseconds a client has to send a whole request (headers and body); a request that is not complete by then is closed. A body of the largest size (about 40 MiB with media) needs a client that uploads faster than 350 KB/s at the default |
| `HTTP_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `30000` | Milliseconds a client has to send the headers of a request; must not be longer than HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS |
| `HTTP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `0` | Milliseconds of silence after which a connection is closed (0 = never). Leave it at 0 or above the longest wait for an answer (about 185 s): a connection that waits for a slow WhatsApp call is silent |
| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | URL | yes |  | Public URL of the gateway, used to build absolute links |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `fatal`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`, `silent` | no | `info` | Minimum level written by the logger |
| `DATABASE_URL` | URL | yes |  | PostgreSQL connection string |
| `REDIS_URL` | URL | yes |  | Redis connection string |
| `REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `15000` | Milliseconds the gateway waits for Redis at start before it exits with an error; once it runs, a lost connection is retried without a limit |
| `ADMIN_API_KEY` | string, 32 characters or more | yes |  | Admin API key, 32 characters or more (stored only as a hash) |
| `METRICS_TOKEN` | string, 32 characters or more | no |  | Bearer token, 32 characters or more, that grants access to GET /metrics; when unset, only an admin key can read it |
| `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_MINUTES` | integer, 0 or more | no | `10` | Minutes the previous API key keeps working after a rotation |
| `API_KEY_MAX_TTL_DAYS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `0` | Longest lifetime in days an API key may be given; 0 means no cap |
| `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `0` | Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted when resolving the client IP; behind a proxy it must be set, or every client shares the proxy address and its rate limit |
| `BULL_BOARD_ENABLED` | `true`, `false` | no | `false` | Serve the BullMQ dashboard to admin keys |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | string | no |  | Comma-separated origins allowed by CORS and Socket.IO; a * is refused in production |
| `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | integer, 1 or more | no | `300` | Requests per minute allowed per API key and, separately, per client address |
| `ENABLE_DOCS` | `true`, `false` | no |  | Serve Swagger UI and the OpenAPI JSON; when unset, true except in production, where true is refused |
| `WWEBJS_DATA_PATH` | string, 1 character or more | no | `./.wwebjs_auth` | Folder where whatsapp-web.js keeps the authenticated sessions. It is created if missing and tested for writing at boot: the gateway does not start when it cannot be used, and /ready goes 503 if it stops being writable |
| `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | Chromium or Chrome binary. Set it: the install does not download one (puppeteer build scripts are off), so a session cannot start without it |
| `WWEB_VERSION` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | Pins the WhatsApp Web version; when unset, the live latest build |
| `WWEB_VERSION_CACHE_TYPE` | `local`, `remote`, `none` | no | `local` | Where the pinned WhatsApp Web HTML snapshot is read from |
| `WWEB_CACHE_PATH` | string, 1 character or more | no | `./.wwebjs_cache` | Folder holding the local WhatsApp Web HTML snapshots |
| `WWEB_VERSION_REMOTE_PATH` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | https URL template of the remote snapshots with a {version} placeholder; required when WWEB_VERSION_CACHE_TYPE is remote. The page it serves runs inside the logged-in browser: trust the host |
| `WWEB_VERSION_STRICT` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Fail the session start when the pinned WhatsApp Web version cannot be loaded, instead of running the live latest build |
| `QR_MAX_RETRIES` | integer, 0 or more | no | `6` | QR codes refreshed before a session gives up pairing (wwebjs shows this number plus one); 0 never gives up and keeps the browser running |
| `TAKEOVER_ON_CONFLICT` | `true`, `false` | no | `false` | Take the session back when WhatsApp Web is opened elsewhere |
| `DEVICE_NAME` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | Device name shown in the linked devices list |
| `BROWSER_NAME` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | Browser name shown in the linked devices list |
| `PROXY_URL` | URL | no |  | Proxy the Chromium traffic goes through (http, https, socks4 or socks5); credentials in the URL work for http and https only; when unset, a direct connection |
| `WA_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `60000` | Milliseconds a call to WhatsApp Web may take before it is abandoned |
| `FFMPEG_PATH` | string, 1 character or more | no |  | ffmpeg binary used to convert media; when unset, the one on the PATH |
| `MAX_SESSIONS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `10` | Sessions the gateway accepts to create |
| `SESSION_START_STAGGER_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `5000` | Milliseconds between the starts of sessions at boot |
| `SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `180000` | Milliseconds a session may take to become ready |
| `SESSION_RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `0` | Reconnection attempts after a disconnect; 0 means unlimited |
| `SESSION_INITIALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `5` | Consecutive failed browser starts of a session before it is marked failed |
| `SESSION_AUTH_QUARANTINE_TTL_DAYS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `7` | Days a saved login that the gateway moved aside (WWEBJS_DATA_PATH/.quarantine) is kept before it is deleted for good |
| `WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `30000` | Milliseconds between health checks of each session |
| `WATCHDOG_MAX_FAILURES` | integer, 1 or more | no | `3` | Consecutive failed health checks before a session is restarted |
| `MEMORY_RESTART_THRESHOLD_MB` | integer, 0 or more | no | `0` | Resident memory in MB of the gateway process plus the browsers of its sessions, above which the largest idle session is restarted; 0 disables the check |
| `INBOUND_ORDERING_ENABLED` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Hold and sort inbound messages per chat |
| `INBOUND_LATE_THRESHOLD_S` | integer, 0 or more | no | `3` | Seconds of difference in sentAt after which a message counts as late |
| `INBOUND_ORDER_WINDOW_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `1500` | Milliseconds the order buffer waits for earlier messages of a chat |
| `INBOUND_ORDER_MAX_HOLD_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `5000` | Longest time in milliseconds a message is held, whatever keeps arriving |
| `INBOUND_ORDER_MAX_MESSAGES` | integer, 1 or more | no | `200` | Messages a chat may hold in the order buffer before it flushes |
| `MESSAGE_BATCH_ENABLED` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Publish the synthesized message_batch event |
| `RECONCILE_ON_READY` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Fetch the recent messages of the busiest chats when a session becomes ready |
| `RECONCILE_MAX_CHATS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `50` | Chats the reconciler visits per session start (0 turns the reconciliation off) |
| `RECONCILE_FETCH_LIMIT` | integer, 1 or more | no | `50` | Messages the reconciler fetches per chat |
| `RECONCILE_LOOKBACK_HOURS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `48` | Hours into the past the reconciler looks for missed messages (0 turns the reconciliation off) |
| `INCLUDE_RAW` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Attach the sanitized raw WhatsApp data to messages |
| `RAW_MAX_FIELD_BYTES` | integer, 1 or more | no | `8192` | Bytes a single field of the raw data may take before it is truncated |
| `SEND_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `1000` | Minimum milliseconds between two sends of the same session |
| `SEND_JITTER_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `400` | Random milliseconds added to the send interval |
| `SEND_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `60000` | Milliseconds a synchronous send request waits for the outcome |
| `SEND_MAX_WAIT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `300000` | Milliseconds an accepted send may wait in the queue before it fails |
| `SEND_NOT_READY_RETRY_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `5000` | Milliseconds before a send is retried while its session is not ready |
| `SEND_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` | integer, 1 or more | no | `5` | Consecutive send failures that open the circuit breaker of a session |
| `SEND_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `60000` | Milliseconds an open circuit breaker stays open |
| `MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` | integer, 1 or more | no | `33554432` | Largest media file in bytes |
| `MEDIA_FETCH_CONCURRENCY` | integer, 1 or more | no | `4` | Media URLs downloaded at the same time (all the sessions together; when they are all busy the next turn goes to the session that has waited longest since its last one); each one can hold up to MAX_MEDIA_BYTES, about three times over while it is converted |
| `MEDIA_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `30000` | Milliseconds the download of a media URL of a send may take |
| `SEND_QUEUE_MAX_PER_SESSION` | integer, 1 or more | no | `500` | Sends a session may have waiting or running in its queue; the next one is refused with 429 SEND_QUEUE_FULL. Redis keeps every job, media included, so the memory this allows is this number times the size of the sends |
| `SEND_QUEUE_MAX_TOTAL` | integer, 1 or more | no | `2000` | Sends all the sessions together may have waiting or running; the next one is refused with 429 SEND_QUEUE_FULL |
| `SEND_ENQUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `5000` | Milliseconds the gateway waits for Redis to accept a send before it answers 503 QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE |
| `CONVERSATION_WINDOW_HOURS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `24` | Hours after the last inbound message during which a chat counts as a conversation |
| `ALLOW_COLD_SENDS` | `true`, `false` | no | `false` | Allow sending to chats without a conversation |
| `COLD_SENDS_PER_DAY` | integer, 0 to 1000 | no | `20` | Cold sends allowed per session per day |
| `COLD_SEND_MIN_GAP_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `60000` | Minimum milliseconds between two cold sends |
| `LOOKUPS_PER_DAY` | integer, 0 to 10000 | no | `100` | Number lookups allowed per session per day |
| `PER_CHAT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `1500` | Minimum milliseconds between two sends to the same chat |
| `PER_CHAT_MAX_PER_MINUTE` | integer, 1 to 60 | no | `10` | Sends per minute to the same chat |
| `SESSION_MAX_PER_MINUTE` | integer, 1 to 600 | no | `20` | Sends per minute of a session |
| `SESSION_MAX_PER_HOUR` | integer, 1 to 10000 | no | `300` | Sends per hour of a session |
| `SESSION_MAX_PER_DAY` | integer, 1 to 100000 | no | `1500` | Sends per day of a session |
| `DUPLICATE_RECIPIENTS_THRESHOLD` | integer, 1 to 10000 | no | `5` | Recipients of the same text inside the window that count as a mass send |
| `DUPLICATE_WINDOW_MINUTES` | integer, 1 to 1440 | no | `10` | Minutes in which identical texts are compared |
| `WARMUP_DAYS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `14` | Days over which a new session ramps up to its full limits |
| `WARMUP_START_FRACTION` | number, 0 to 1 | no | `0.1` | Fraction of the limits a session starts with on its first day |
| `UNREACHABLE_STREAK` | integer, 1 to 100 | no | `5` | Consecutive unanswered sends that mark a recipient as unreachable |
| `UNREACHABLE_MIN_AGE_HOURS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `72` | Hours a send must remain unanswered before it counts toward the unreachable streak |
| `SEND_POLICY_MAX_WAIT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `1800000` | Longest milliseconds the send policy may delay a message |
| `HEALTH_WINDOW` | integer, 1 to 10000 | no | `50` | Recent sends the session health score uses |
| `HEALTH_MIN_SAMPLES` | integer, 1 to 10000 | no | `10` | Results the health score needs before it can pause a session (at most HEALTH_WINDOW counts) |
| `HEALTH_MAX_BAD_RATIO` | number, 0 to 1 | no | `0.2` | Ratio of bad outcomes in the window that pauses the session |
| `HEALTH_COOLDOWN_MIN` | integer, 0 or more | no | `30` | Minutes a session stays paused after a bad window |
| `HUMANIZE_MIN_REPLY_DELAY_MS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `1500` | Minimum milliseconds between an inbound message and the reply to it |
| `EVENT_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS` | integer, 0 or more | no | `300` | Seconds of past events a reconnecting socket may replay |
| `WEBHOOKS_MAX_PER_SESSION` | integer, 1 or more | no | `20` | Webhooks a session can have, and as many for those of every session; creating one past it is refused |
| `WEBHOOK_TEST_MAX_PER_MINUTE` | integer, 1 or more | no | `6` | Test pings (POST /v1/webhooks/:id/test) a webhook accepts per minute; one more is refused with 429 RATE_LIMITED. Each one is a signed request to the URL of the webhook |
| `WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `10000` | Milliseconds a webhook endpoint has to answer |
| `WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `10` | Delivery attempts per webhook event |
| `WEBHOOK_BACKOFF_MS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `5000` | Milliseconds before the first webhook retry; later retries back off exponentially |
| `WEBHOOK_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | integer, 1 or more | no | `10` | Webhook deliveries in parallel |
| `WEBHOOK_INLINE_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` | integer, 0 or more | no | `5242880` | Largest media in bytes a webhook carries inline; larger media goes by URL |
| `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST` | string | no |  | Comma-separated hosts exempt from the private-address check of webhook URLs; a range that covers every address (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) is refused in production |
| `ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOK_TARGETS` | `true`, `false` | no | `false` | Allow webhook URLs that resolve to private addresses; development only, refused in production |
| `MEDIA_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST` | string | no |  | Comma-separated hosts a send may download media from although they are private. Empty by default and apart from WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST: the media URL comes from the caller of a send, and the file is sent on to a WhatsApp chat, so any host listed here can be read by every key that may send. A range that covers every address (/0) is refused in production |
| `CALL_CACHE_SIZE` | integer, 1 or more | no | `50` | Recent calls kept in memory to reject them |
| `DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `14` | Days webhook deliveries are kept before they are deleted |
| `MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` | integer, 1 or more | no | `30` | Days messages are kept before they are deleted |
| `STORE_MESSAGE_BODIES` | `true`, `false` | no | `true` | Store the text of messages, not only their metadata |
